turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, I came in today because my mind just feels... foggy lately. I work at the library, and recently I can't even seem to keep my place in my old cataloguing notes. It's frustrating because I just sit there and can't even decide what simple thing to do next. It's making my day-to-day pretty difficult.

symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient explicitly describes having a foggy mind, difficulty concentrating on cataloguing notes, and indecisiveness about what to do next.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don't?
turns.patient_response: No, no, nothing like that. I haven't seen or heard anything unusual. It's really just the trouble focusing and getting my work done that's been bothering me.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient mentions having trouble focusing and getting work done, indicating difficulty sustaining attention on tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies seeing or hearing anything unusual.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I have. Um, most days lately I just... I sit at the kitchen table and it feels like the color has just gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books—I just look at them and they make me feel heavy instead of interested. It's just a very flat, heavy feeling.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient confirms feeling down, describing a 'flat, heavy feeling' and stating that 'the color has just gone out of everything'.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly notes a loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, stating that their old watercolor books now make them feel heavy instead of interested.

turns.doctor_question: Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I suppose I have. Like I was just saying about the watercolor books... I used to really enjoy sitting down and painting, but lately, I just don't have the desire to even pick up a brush. I haven't really noticed it with much else, just that I don't really care to do the few things I used to do for fun.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly confirms losing interest in activities they used to enjoy, such as painting, stating they no longer have the desire to do them.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been feeling this way?
turns.patient_response: Well, I'd say it's been about three months now. Most days, anyway. That low mood and the fogginess with my focus... it all really started right around the time I began preparing to leave my job at the library.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly mentions experiencing a 'low mood' most days for the past three months.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient describes experiencing 'fogginess with my focus', indicating diminished ability to concentrate or clouded thinking.

turns.doctor_question: Did these feelings begin after a particular stressful event in your life?
turns.patient_response: Not really, no. I mean, besides leaving the library like I mentioned, nothing else was going on. And even that wasn't really a bad stress, it was just a change. So, no, there wasn't any sort of big crisis or anything that set it off. It just sort of... crept up on me.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient explicitly denies that their feelings were triggered by a particular stressful event or crisis.

turns.doctor_question: Before this started three months ago, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for days or weeks at a time?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had days where I felt a bit down or tired, just like anyone else, but nothing that lasted for weeks or felt quite like this heavy fog. This is the first time I've really dealt with something like this.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been worrying a lot more than usual lately?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I'm concerned about how I'm feeling, obviously, because I'm not used to this... but I wouldn't say I'm pacing the floors or agonizing over things. Just the normal amount of worry, I suppose.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying more than usual, stating they only have a normal amount of worry.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient denies pacing the floors, indicating a lack of physical restlessness or tension.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological condition that affects your memory or thinking?
turns.patient_response: No, nothing like that. I've never been diagnosed with any kind of neurological condition or memory problem. My physical health is pretty standard for my age, really, so... no, nothing along those lines.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been waking up much earlier than usual lately?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, actually, I have. I go to bed tired, but then I end up waking up around four in the morning. I can't get back to sleep after that, so I just lie there... thinking about what I am supposed to do with myself now.

symptom_reasoning.S027: The patient confirms waking up unusually early (around 4 AM) and being unable to return to sleep, which is a clear indication of early morning awakening, a subtype of sleep disturbance.
